answer:
**The split the ruling asks for.** Time has two halves. *Showing or hiding* is a visual: a pure function of the datum's text, the instant it shows until, and the instant of the render. *Knowing when something arrived and asking for a repaint when the display will change* is data: the store already holds the clock and the scheduler the root injects (D2, D-a), and the store spec already says the store requests its own repaints. So the visual decides, the store remembers and repaints, and no instrument subscribes, polls or keeps time.

**(1) The visual: `extensions/jefferson/components/visuals/timed.ts`**, beside `bar.ts`, importing no file of this package (the rule `bar.ts` already obeys). One export:
```
/** The text while the render's instant is before the datum's shown-until instant; unknown after it, or when either instant is missing. */
export function timed(text: string, shownUntil: number | undefined, now: number | undefined): string | undefined
```
It renders the text or nothing, and nothing is `undefined` so the cell treats a hidden datum as unknown and drops its label and gap (statusline spec, 'An unknown datum suppresses the label'). It has no configuration of its own, as the bar has none: the duration is the datum's, not the visual's.

**How an instrument composes it.** A declaration field, because the whole datum shows or hides, not a piece of its prose (which is what `$bar` places): `InstrumentDeclaration.shownUntil?: (readings: Readings) => number | undefined` — the reading that carries the instant the datum shows until. The binding applies it after the format resolves: `const text = resolveFormat(…); return declaration.shownUntil === undefined ? text : timed(text, declaration.shownUntil(readings), readings.sampledAt) ?? "";`. Any instrument that declares `shownUntil` is timed; the notice declares `shownUntil: readings => readings.notice?.shownUntil` and nothing else about time. The import rule moves one notch: `components/visuals/` files import nothing of the package, and any `components/` file or `format.ts` may import them (today only `format.ts` reaches `bar.ts`); that is the layout spec's 'Imports between the homes run one way' and an ADR 0009 addendum, and it is what 'composable into an instrument' means in the tree.

**(2) Where time lives.** The root keeps injecting `now` (`performance.now`) and `schedule` into the store (D2 unchanged). The store, on a push of a timed datum, stamps `shownUntil = now() + holdMs` once — the one home of the deadline — and arms one repaint at it with the early-fire re-arm as built; the callback *only* requests the repaint and no longer clears anything. Every `sample()` carries `sampledAt: number | undefined` (`now()` read once per render, `undefined` after dispose), which is the 'as of this render' instant the visual compares against — so two timed cells in one render agree, per the store's one-state rule. The store never hides: it holds the datum and its `shownUntil` until a newer one replaces it or the session is replaced. `Readings.notice` becomes `Timed<Notice>` where `type Timed<T> = T & { readonly shownUntil: number }` is declared in `session-data-store.ts` for the next timed datum to reuse. Nothing in `components/` reads a clock; `imports.mjs`'s `CLOCK` rule stays as is.

**(3) What moves, what stays.** *Store:* remove the sample-time drop (`now() >= deadline` block) and the callback's `notice = undefined; deadline = undefined`; keep the slot, `showNotice` (now stamping `shownUntil`), `armExpiry`, `cancelNotice`, the three events, dispose. *`data/notice.ts`:* unchanged as the rule, plus the already-ruled bare values — `$blocks` the bare count with `thinking`/`thinkingOne` kinds, `$idle` the bare minutes — and `format.ts`'s generalized escape with the `missIdle` default `Cache miss after $idle\m idle`. *Notice instrument:* gains `shownUntil`; `composed`, `variableFg`, `NOTICE_SECONDS`, `seconds`/`formats` options stay. *Binding:* one `timed` call after `resolveFormat`; the composed step is untouched. *Feed, gate (D3), reader:* unchanged; `noticeSeconds` still flows root → store, converted to ms once in the store. *New:* `components/visuals/timed.ts` and its test.

**(4) `seconds` stays the instrument's option** (`instruments.notice.seconds`, 1..60, default 10 in `notice.ts`), because the visual has no configuration surface and Joel's ruling configures an instrument once by name; the duration is how long *this instrument's datum* shows, and the root hands it to the store for that datum. The config surface does not change. A second timed instrument declares its own `seconds` and `shownUntil` the same way; the reader's notice-specific gate (D3) is about the notice's *events*, not the visual, and is not generalized now (don't invent).

**(5) Decisions, specs and tests that move.**
- *design.md:* D1 — `Readings.notice: Timed<Notice>`; D2 — strike 'drops the notice when a read begins and `now() >= deadline`' and the callback's drop; the clock still decides, through `sampledAt`, in the visual; D5 — add `shownUntil` and the binding's `timed` application; fold in the bare-values ruling (`thinkingOne`, bare `$idle`, `\m`); new **D10 — the timed visual** (contract above, file, import rule, why a declaration field and not a format variable: the datum hides whole, and Joel ruled time out of the format language); D7 — 'replaces' now means a new `shownUntil` and a cancelled repaint, no drop; D8/D9 — below, and a third ADR: *a visual is a pure part under `components/visuals/`, mixed in by a declaration or a format, never holding time or a host handle*.
- *session-data-store delta:* 'A notice expires on a clock' becomes 'A timed datum carries the instant it shows until, and the store requests one repaint when that instant passes' — the store MUST hold the datum and `shownUntil`, MUST sample `sampledAt` once per render, MUST request exactly one repaint at `shownUntil` (re-arming on an early fire), and MUST NOT hide the datum. 'No notice is showing → unknown' narrows to 'no notice has arrived, or the session was replaced'; a passed `shownUntil` is the statusline's concern.
- *statusline delta:* new requirement 'A timed visual shows and hides a datum' — `components/visuals/timed.ts` imports nothing; text while `sampledAt < shownUntil`; unknown at or after, label included; the `notice` instrument composes it through `shownUntil`; 'No notice to show' and 'A notice beside a fill cell' cite it. Plus the bare-values and escape scenarios already ruled.
- *extension-source-layout delta:* 'The bar has its own file' generalizes to 'Each visual has its own file under `components/visuals/` and imports nothing of the package; `components/` files and `format.ts` may import a visual.'
- *Tests that move:* store 3.6 ('a read past the deadline drops the notice') is deleted and its boundary moves to `tests/timed.test.ts` (`now = until − 1` shows, `now = until` hides, `undefined` either side hides; red: the comparison flipped); store 3.5 becomes 'expiry requests exactly one repaint and the sample still carries the notice with its `shownUntil`'; 3.7 early fire stays; a binding/instrument test 'a timed instrument renders nothing, label included, once its shown-until instant has passed' (red: the `timed` call removed from the binding); the e2e `jefferson.test.ts` notice test gains 'after the visible time the line no longer carries `Notice:`' using the fake host's clock if it has one, else stays as is; store sample test gains `sampledAt` to its keys. Everything else (`data/notice.ts` boundaries, feed, gate, configuration, alignment, fill cell) stands.

This is the smallest shape that is genuinely reusable: one pure function, one declaration field, one store type, one import-rule sentence, and the deadline computed in one place.
decided_by: Joel's 2026-11-10 ruling 'What the timed part is' (owner-rulings.md): the show-and-hide is a visual under components/visuals/, reusable and composable into an instrument, not baked into the notice; his bar ruling in ADR 0009 ('It most definitely doesn't go in format… a component that an instrument can mix in… independent of anything else's responsibility') fixes the visual's shape as a pure part importing nothing; the living store spec's 'the store requests a repaint itself' and 'every read in one render observes one state' place the clock, the scheduler and `sampledAt` in the store; my PL4 ruling D-a keeps `now`/`schedule` injected at the root; the 2026-11-05 ruling that an instrument is configured once by name keeps `seconds` on the instrument. The bare-values shape is my consult ruling and Joel's 'Generalize the escape'.
follow_up: The one place a reader may push back: the store still knows the deadline (it stamps `shownUntil` and schedules the repaint), so 'time' is not wholly in the visual. It cannot be: an instrument may not subscribe or poll, a render may not request a repaint, and the store is the only party holding the scheduler. If Joel would rather the store know nothing of durations, the alternative is the binding holding `seconds` and the store exposing a generic 'repaint me at instant T' request from the root — more mechanism for the same behaviour. Does the store stamping `shownUntil` and requesting the one repaint satisfy 'don't bake the visual into the instrument'? I say yes: the instrument and the visual know nothing of timers, and that is the abstraction he asked for.
